newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine fixed income market ready to grow.
newsitem.headline: Philippine fixed income market ready to grow.

text.p: The outlook for the Philippine fixed income market looks bright with the country's recent credit upgrade and better economic fundamentals of low inflation and budget surpluses, bankers said on Wednesday.
The supply of possible issuers is also expected to pick up especially from infrastructure projects, they said.

"With most corporations already maturing into their business cycles, and new entities venturing into capital intensive infrastructure projects, the practicality of raising capital through debts, specifically longer-tenored papers has now become more pronounced," said Helen Alvarez, research director of All Asia Capital and Trust Corp told a conference.

The fixed income market was worth 555 billion pesos or $21 billion by the end of last year, equivalent to roughly 25 percent of the 1996 gdp, Alvarez said. The figure includes domestic and overseas issues.
However, much needs to be done to develop the secondary market, participants at the conference said.
Cristina Orbeta, Central Bank director for the management of external debt, said the undeveloped secondary market has led Philippine borrowers to continue to prefer to go overseas.
Constraints on the development of the domestic bond market include tax regulations and a lack of trading facilities such as an efficient bond registration process.
"The ability of Philippine issuers to tap the international capital markets for long-dated bonds speaks well of the growing acceptability of Philippine risks offshore," Orbeta said.
"At the same time, it underscored the inability of the domestic capital market to satisfy demand for financing at the desired terms," she added.

National Treasurer Caridad Valdehuesa said the secondary market, which has a daily average turnover of 250 billion pesos, could soon have an electronic trading system to make a transparent and efficient treasuries market.

She added the Bureau of Treasury has discarded the idea of listing government securities on the Philippine Stock Exchange to protect Treasruy bond prices from the volatile cycle of the equities market.
"We aim for stability of our T-bond prices while enhancing their liquidity," she said.
